name: Question 5
problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
5{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+15x{y}^{′}+25y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y=\frac{{c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}{x},
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
5{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+15x{y}^{′}+25y=0,\,y(1)=1,\,{y}^{′}(1)=3,\,x>0.
$$
worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(1)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
1={c}_{1}.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=3,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =-{x}^{-2}(({c}_{1}-2{c}_{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+(2{c}_{1}+{c}_{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x))).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute ${y}^{′}(1)=3$ and ${c}_{1}=1$ into the above to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =-(1-2{c}_{2}) \\ {c}_{2} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(x)=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}{x}.
$$

Question 5
?

Given that the differential equation 5x2y″+15xy′+25y=0 has the general solution y=c1cos⁡(2ln⁡x)+c2sin⁡(2ln⁡x)x, solve the initial value problem 5x2y″+15xy′+25y=0,y(1)=1,y′(1)=3,x>0.

a
 y(x)=cos⁡(2ln⁡x)+2sin⁡(2ln⁡x)x
b
 y(x)=2cos⁡(2ln⁡x)+sin⁡(2ln⁡x)x
c
 y(x)=cos⁡(ln⁡x)+2sin⁡(ln⁡x)x
d
 y(x)=2cos⁡(2ln⁡x)+2sin⁡(2ln⁡x)x
e
 y(x)=cos⁡(2ln⁡x)−2sin⁡(2ln⁡x)x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We find the constants c1 and c2 using the initial conditions.

  • Substituting y(1)=1 into the general solution gives 1=c1.

  • To apply the condition y′(1)=3, we first differentiate y to get y′(x)=−x−2((c1−2c2)cos⁡(2ln⁡x)+(2c1+c2)sin⁡(2ln⁡(x))). Then, we substitute y′(1)=3 and c1=1 into the above to get 3=−(1−2c2)c2=2.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is y(x)=cos⁡(2ln⁡x)+2sin⁡(2ln⁡x)x.
